summary: The flow reads an untrusted line from the console in 73a.bad(), stores it in a LinkedList, and passes it to 73b.badSink(), which concatenates it directly into an OS command string executed via Runtime.exec() (on Windows via cmd.exe /c, where shell metacharacters are interpreted). This allows OS command injection (CWE-78). The fix validates the decoded argument against a strict allowlist of characters valid for a file/directory argument before executing, following the pattern of the Tomcat CVE-2019-0232 repair (validate the decoded argument against a platform-safe pattern and reject otherwise). Legitimate directory/file arguments (letters, digits, '.', '_', '/', '\\', ':', '-') still work; inputs containing spaces, ';', '&', '|', '`', '$', redirection or other metacharacters are rejected, neutralizing argument and command injection without disabling the feature.
